description: Section 214(b) of the Immigration and Nationality Act presumes intending immigration. The officer does not have to prove the applicant will overstay; the applicant has to prove he will not, which is a negative about the future.
energy_note: Proving what you are not going to do.

aspect: EXAMPLE - how much of the refusal stream it is
description: Practitioner estimates put 214(b) at roughly 89% of all B-1/B-2 refusals issued to Mexican nationals at US consulates in Mexico. It is described as the most common US visa refusal in the world.
energy_note: Nine refusals in ten are this one clause.
notes: The 89% figure is from an immigration law firm, not State Department data. State publishes adjusted refusal rates by nationality annually; that is the citable source.

description: The MRV fee buys an interview, not a visa, and is not refunded on refusal. Reapplying means paying it again, with no waiting period required and no limit on attempts - and no reason to expect a different answer on the same evidence.
energy_note: Paying again for the same answer.

aspect: The 'weak ties' profile is the modern working life
description: Refusals cluster on: work that does not require physical presence (commission sales, gig work, remote contracting), renting rather than owning, and family who could plausibly relocate too. A young man with a laptop and a rented room is the profile.
energy_note: Punished for having a job that does not tie him to a building.

aspect: Money in the account is read against you either way
description: Too little and there are insufficient funds. A single large deposit and it looks arranged for the application. There is no published balance that suffices, because the standard is the officer's overall impression.
energy_note: No number he could have put in the account.

description: He has the property deed, the employment letter, the bank statements and the return ticket. The officer asks three questions, none about any of it, and slides a blue sheet under the glass. Total elapsed time at the window: under four minutes. The queue behind him is 300 people long.
energy_note: Four minutes, and the folder never opened.

aspect: The refusal is remembered by the next officer
description: Prior refusals are visible in the system at every subsequent application, so a single 214(b) becomes a fact about him that he carries into every future interview, in any category.
energy_note: One no, quoted back at him for twenty years.

aspect: It is the hurdle the game should open with
description: For the Mexican difficulty setting this is the natural first gate: cheap to explain, instantly legible, and it produces the correct feeling - that he did everything asked and it did not matter.
energy_note: He did everything right. It did not matter.
notes: Design note for the journey scenes.
